*   # Who’s Selling French Debt?

    [From robinjbrooks.substack.com](https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/whos-selling-french-debt)

    [![](https://assets.faireconomy.media/nfs/npd/2017/06/06/npd_19_50_21.v2.jpg)](https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/whos-selling-french-debt)

    https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/whos-selling-french-debt

    When bad things happen in government bond markets - the recent rise in French yields most definitely belongs in this category - there’s always lots of finger-pointing about who’s responsible. This’ll typically involve individual transactions that are said to have moved the market - this Bloomberg story on a Japanese asset manager selling out of their French holdings made lots of waves - but this really makes no sense. Debt markets are massive, so who’s to know whether it was this particular thing that moved markets or some other transaction? In the end, instead of scapegoating investors, the blame belongs to ... This author slays the incorrect perception of the existence of hostile bond vigilantes.

"Debt markets are massive, so who’s to know whether it was this particular thing that moved markets or some other transaction? In the end, instead of scapegoating investors, the blame belongs to policy makers for running endlessly reckless fiscal policy. The main culprit for the French debt sell-off is France itself."

This is not confined to France but also to any other country that is so fiscally irresponsible as to find their bond market collapsing.
